title: vLLM multimodal embeddings -- T1499 unvalidated sparse tensor indices crash or corrupt memory
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-56340 (GHSA-mcmc-2m55-j8jj,
CVSS 8.7 HIGH), affecting vLLM >= 0.10.2 and < 0.13.0.

vLLM's multimodal embeddings processing (the `prompt-embeds` feature)
is missing sparse tensor validation. Because PyTorch disables sparse
tensor invariant checks by default, an attacker who submits a crafted
embedding request with MALFORMED tensor indices (negative or
out-of-bounds) reaches the tensor operations unchecked -- triggering
crashes or resource exhaustion at minimum, with the advisory noting
POTENTIAL for out-of-bounds/write-what-where memory corruption beyond
denial of service. This is explicitly a continuation of an EARLIER bug
(CVE-2025-62164), whose prior fix only disabled the `prompt-embeds`
feature by default rather than fixing the missing validation itself --
any deployment that re-enables the feature (a documented, supported
configuration) is exposed again.

Detection logic flags a request to a prompt-embeds-enabled endpoint
whose embedding payload declares sparse tensor indices outside the
expected non-negative, in-bounds range -- the specific malformed-index
shape this advisory's root cause requires, distinct from an ordinary
well-formed embedding request.

Aggregated from 2 independent sources (vLLM's own GHSA advisory +
VulnCheck's corroborating write-up, both citing the prior
CVE-2025-62164 the incomplete fix stems from), fixed with root-cause
index validation (not merely a feature-default flip this time).
